detailed_analysis.radiology_interpretation_assessment: This OSCE station (White Coat Hypertension) is NOT appropriate for radiology interpretation evaluation. White coat hypertension is diagnosed via ambulatory BP monitoring (ABPM) or home BP readings - NOT radiological imaging. The 'images' listed (BP readings, ABPM data) are clinical measurements, not CXR/CT/MRI/ultrasound. A radiology expert would have NO role in this station. This represents a fundamental category error in OSCE design.
detailed_analysis.systematic_approach_explanation: No systematic radiology interpretation framework present (no ABCDE for CXR, no ABC for CT, no 7-step ECG analysis). Content is generic placeholder text without any actual clinical findings to interpret systematically.
detailed_analysis.australian_terminology_notes: References cite Australian textbooks (Talley & O'Connor, John Murtagh) but actual content is templates without Australia-specific terms (should use 'hypertension clinic', 'Medicare item 10997 for ABPM', 'Heart Foundation guidelines 2016'). Generic BP/ABPM terminology used.
detailed_analysis.critical_findings_identified: N/A - no actual investigation results provided to interpret
detailed_analysis.clinical_correlation: Poor - vital signs (BP 140/90) contradict diagnosis (white coat HTN requires normal ambulatory BP). No correlation between stated diagnosis and presented findings.
detailed_analysis.australian_guidelines_referenced: Citations present but irrelevant (Antenatal Guidelines for hypertension topic, obesity management sections for white coat HTN)
detailed_analysis.amc_clinical_exam_alignment: Poor - tasks are generic templates not aligned with AMC cardiology/imaging stations. AMC would expect: ECG interpretation (STEMI recognition), CXR systematic review (pulmonary oedema in HF), Echo valve assessment (AS grading), not ABPM interpretation for white coat HTN.
detailed_analysis.educational_value: Very low due to placeholder content. Cannot be used for AMC preparation without complete rewrite with actual clinical scenarios, real investigation findings, and specialty-appropriate tasks.
